body:
## Destination

An agreed spec at `.scratch/entity-models/spec.md`, published as a `spec` issue and ready to split into implementation tickets. It defines entities that switch representation between their icon and a 3D model based on distance from the camera.

## Notes

- Planning only. Produce decisions, not production code. Prototypes are throwaway.
- Agreed while charting on 2026-10-03:
  - Representation switching only. Each entity stays one entity at every distance.
  - Only entities can have models. Ordinary point features keep icons.
  - Vocabulary: **Icon**, **Model**, **Representation** and **Heading**, as defined in [CONTEXT.md](https://github.com/the-Drunken-coder/Ridgeline/blob/main/CONTEXT.md). The glossary edit is pending on the working branch until it is committed.
  - Switching is per entity by distance from the camera. It has a dead zone to prevent flicker and one consumer-tunable threshold.
  - Between far and close, models are tentatively enlarged to a fixed screen size and grow to real size when very close. The prototype confirms this.
  - An entity without a heading stays an icon at every distance and reports a diagnostic.
  - Heading is required. Pitch and roll are optional, for aircraft.
  - Consumers supply and register model files, as with icons. Ridgeline ships no models. The playground uses freely licensed samples.
  - Workload target: up to 1,000 entities shown as icons and up to 100 showing models at once.
- Technical calls (renderer, loader, dependencies) are delegated to the agent. Constraint: no full 3D engine such as three.js. Bring one recommendation with its tradeoffs, not an API menu.
- Visual choices are the user's. Show a prototype and wait for their choice before fixing a look.
- Consumers own workflows and selection under [consumer-owned workflows](https://github.com/the-Drunken-coder/Ridgeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0001-consumer-owned-workflows.md). Check [MapLibre extension access](https://github.com/the-Drunken-coder/Ridgeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-maplibre-extension-access.md) when choosing the renderer.
- Related behavior: [airborne entities](https://github.com/the-Drunken-coder/Ridgeline/blob/main/.scratch/airborne-entities/spec.md) and the [reliability repairs](https://github.com/the-Drunken-coder/Ridgeline/blob/main/.scratch/codebase-reliability-repairs/spec.md), especially world copies and the date line.
- Skills: matt-grilling with matt-domain-modeling for human decisions, matt-research for research, and matt-prototype for visual exploration. Read [CODE_CONVENTIONS.md](https://github.com/the-Drunken-coder/Ridgeline/blob/main/CODE_CONVENTIONS.md) before any prototype code.

## Decisions so far

- [Can MapLibre 6.11 draw entity models?](https://github.com/the-Drunken-coder/Ridgeline/issues/72): no native model support; models must be drawn in Ridgeline's own 3D custom layer, reusing its projection, precision and date-line handling, with Ridgeline computing screen size and picking.
- [Choose a lightweight glTF loading approach](https://github.com/the-Drunken-coder/Ridgeline/issues/73): a minimal in-house GLB parser (about 2.7 KB gzip) covered every free vehicle sample tested; libraries add 13 to 50 KB gzip, mostly for features outside that subset. Draco, meshopt, KTX2, skins, morphs and non-GLB files are rejected by name.
- [Find freely licensed sample models](https://github.com/the-Drunken-coder/Ridgeline/issues/74): free low-poly GLBs exist for a drone, two tanks, a plane and a boat; most are CC-BY 3.0 via Poly Pizza and need attribution, the Kenney boat is CC0 after one repackaging pass, and Quaternius is avoided because its license now forbids redistribution.
- [Choose how Ridgeline draws and loads models](https://github.com/the-Drunken-coder/Ridgeline/issues/75): a second Ridgeline custom layer sharing the entity layer's projection code draws each model type once per material, with screen size and box picking on the CPU; an in-house GLB subset parser on the main thread; about 7 to 11 KB gzip, no new dependency. Consumers keep models light under a documented triangle guideline.

## Not yet specified

- **Consumer API.** How consumers register models, give an entity both an icon and a model, tune the switching threshold, and supply heading, pitch and roll. Research found models vary from 7 cm to 25.7 m and may not face the same way, so per-model scale and heading offset are likely needed; many free models also reference external textures. Also which diagnostics apply, for example when a model fails to load. Depends on how Ridgeline draws models and on the prototype.
- **Interaction with models.** Hit testing against a model's shape or its screen area, what the radial picker shows for entities with models, and where labels, ground lines and attachments sit relative to an enlarged model.
- **Slope following** for ground vehicles, revisited after the prototype shows whether flat tanks look wrong on terrain.
- **Projection edge cases:** globe projection, world copies and the date line for models, given the recent reliability repairs in those areas.
- **Verification:** how the spec proves the workload target, and which browsers models must support (the packaged suite covers only Chromium with software WebGL).

## Out of scope

- Grouping units into one higher-level symbol when zoomed out.
- Animated model parts such as rotors.
- Placing or editing models with the drawing tools.
- Touch input.
- Models for ordinary point features.
- Automatic simplified versions of heavy models for distant views: consumers keep models light instead, per [Choose how Ridgeline draws and loads models](https://github.com/the-Drunken-coder/Ridgeline/issues/75).
- Production implementation during this wayfinding effort.
title: Entity models and representation switching
